South of a line near the 29°22′30″ latitude, saline water is encountered in the Georgetown. This is probably caused by a facies change in the Kiamichi - from limestone and shale with solutioned breccia north of the line to shale, gypsum, and anhydrite south of the line.
2.10 Yields vary widely in the aquifer because of the nature of the permeability. Although the limestones are dense and practically impermeable, permeability is derived from the interconnected solution widened openings along faults, joints and fractures. Reeves and Small (1973) observed that "although there are many openings in the subsurface, the chance of finding a large one in any one hole below the potentiometric surface is not good, as indicated by the very few large capacity wells and the many very small capacity wells. In the course of field work, some of the ranchers reported that several borings were drilled before obtaining a well having an adequate capacity." Yields of wells in Val Verde County vary from a few gallons per minute (gpm) to over 1,000 gpm. Specific capacities (yield per foot of drawdown) of tested wells vary from less than 1 to over 30 gpm/ft. Regional movement of ground water is down the dip of the aquifer to the southeast, from recharge areas north of Val Verde County to springs along the Rio Grande and its tributaries. A minor amount of ground water is withdrawn from wells. In 1969 about 1,850 acre feet of ground water were pumped in Val Verde County for all purposes. During the period 1961-67, the average annual spring flow in the county was 502,000 acre feet (Reeves and Small, 1973). Recharge is provided from rainfall on the outcrop and occasionally by loss of stream flow into solutioned openings. The Georgetown outcrop surface is dotted with sinkholes which generally occur along solutioned joints or faults or at joint intersections.

2.12 Mineral Fuel Deposits. Cannel coals which occur in the Laredo formation near Santo Tomas in Webb County were mined for about 50 years. These coals have a high volatile matter content and yield a significant amount of oil and gas when distilled, but they also have a high sulfur content.
